record.context_brief: disk topology from one-sided convex boundary
record.original_question: Let C be a simple closed convex curve in a plane P, and let Sigma be a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface in R^3 with boundary C. If Sigma lies on one side of P, must Sigma be a topological disk?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4 (4*). Let C be a simple closed convex curve in a plane P. Let Sigma be a compact embedded cmc surface in R3 with partial Sigma = C. Assuming that Sigma lies in one side of P, is Sigma a topological disk?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a plane and let $C \subset P$ be a simple closed convex curve. Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature with boundary $\partial \Sigma = C$, and suppose that $\Sigma$ is contained in one of the two closed half-spaces of $\mathbb{R}^3$ determined by $P$. Must $\Sigma$ be a topological disk?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether a compact embedded CMC surface in R^3 with simple closed convex planar boundary, lying entirely on one side of the boundary plane, must be a topological disk is a well-known long-standing problem in the theory of CMC surfaces (classically associated with conjectures of Meeks and others). Web search did not produce a definitive resolution; partial results exist (e.g., for graphs, for small mean curvature, or under additional symmetry/stability assumptions), but the general case appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space
status_evidence.snippet: Compact CMC surfaces with non-empty boundary exist, with the geometry of the boundary imposing geometrical restrictions on the surface.
status_evidence.claim: The topology of compact CMC surfaces with prescribed planar convex boundary is a classical open question in the field, with only partial results available.
